main_text.l: Occurrit mihi hic admodum lepida & facete tofa hiftoria, de perfido quodam Iudeo à pagano quodam huius loci, anno 1604. emturo vinum, Is vinariam cellam pagani ingressus, vina eius vendibilia, quae peculiaribus in dolis feorfim re- ponsa continuebantur, degustans inter pituitandi elegit dolium cotinens potus ex fele&u pomum ob- mas 4. Piganus, vix fore exi&imans, ut Iudeus hunc, cuius perfidia & impostura toti vicinia erat nota & permissa, dolo circumveniret, confirmando, de pretio consensus, Iudeus vinum ex pomis, quod principii vel potius stupido sup- pius palato magis placuerat, letus ad suos defer- ri cura, gloriam non defiles, miserere fraudis illum paganum a fe deceptum effecit, emptus fe pro tolerabili pretio vinum, quo vix praestan- tius aliud. Verum praestanti illo vino acorem acquirens & mucorem (quod facile ex dolio vel non ufqueque, pleno, veletiam non probe occlu- fo contingere potuit, vel etiam, si doli ano exque- fire plena, alio quam ipsa continent liquore, ope- rantur) cum fe deceptum intelligeret, paganis perfidia & malitia incufat. Venum est ad ina- dicem, actum est, pronunciatum, Iudeus damnatum vinum retinere, quod ipse fibi ex multis aliis elegerat, iura coegerunt. Hactenus de Iudeo, nunc adrem.

page.notes: Printing is dense and damaged along the right edge and at the fold; many words in the last lines and the right-hand fragments are only partly legible. Where the scan is too faint to read letter by letter I have not supplied words beyond what is visible, and the transcription above should be treated as a provisional reading. Several Latin words in the middle lines (e.g. "pituitandi", "ponsa", "fele&u") are doubtful and are not marked individually because the scan does not allow a reliable check. The large letter at the start of the first paragraph is not a woodcut initial. No marginal notes are clearly legible. The left-margin catchword/heading "Lepida hiftoria de Iudeo feipsum decipi ente" is a printed running side-title and is not transcribed as main text.
